why: TWO UNCONFIRMED RULING PACKETS CARRY A `what_dies` LIST THAT WOULD BREAK THE SYSTEM IF EXECUTED. decisions/2026-08-05-the-file-path-is-the-link and its -rescoped successor both name cairn/cairn/tools/base/probe.py in what_dies. The ruling door treats what_dies as LITERAL DELETION — ruling.py's verify emits 'STILL ALIVE: <path> was ruled dead and is on disk', and that tooth exists specifically to catch a file coming back. But probe.py is not a file that dies; it is the Probe primitive, imported by live code. Deleting it stops the system. The rulings' actual content is about a probe's POINTER being a file path rather than an id — which is an EDIT to probe.py, not its removal. HYPOTHESIS, and it is labelled as one (Law 3): what_dies was populated with every file the ruling TOUCHES rather than every file the ruling KILLS. The two lists are not the same list, and the schema offers only one of them. THE LIVED SYMPTOM, and why this is filed rather than fixed: tomorrow morning Akien runs `cairn ruling confirm 2026-08-05-the-file-path-is-the-link-rescoped`, because the reading in it is correct and he agrees with it. The packet is then green and authoritative, and it instructs whoever acts on it to delete nine files, one of which eight modules import. The confirm step reads now_the_spec_says, which is right; nothing shows him the what_dies list is wrong. CC WILL NOT ACT ON THIS: an unconfirmed ruling is not a resting authority, and the fix touches Akien's own packets.

occurrences.how_found: `cairn ruling list` 2026-08-05 evening, during the overnight wrap: both packets print STILL ALIVE warnings for nine paths. Read as a report about the DISK, they say the ruling was not carried out. Read against the disk, they say the ruling should not be carried out.

measured_evidence.the_other_eight_paths: the four skills/*/probes/*_door_refusals.py, cairn/tools/base/probes/does_optional_mean_never_carried.py, cairn/bin/probes/retention_window.py, cairn/launchers/probes/reported_but_unfixed_floor.py and cairn/cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_probe_carry.py are all on disk and all referenced. Whether each is edit-not-delete was NOT individually verified — only probe.py was, and one counterexample is enough to make the list unsafe to execute wholesale.
measured_evidence.not_verified: whether the ruling AUTHOR (CC, at intake) intended deletion for any of the nine. The packets carry the_ruling_verbatim; nobody has re-read Akien's actual words against the nine paths. That re-read is the first act of resolving this, and it is his to do or to delegate.

resolution_paths: A: the packets are AMENDED before confirm — what_dies keeps only genuinely dying files, and the touched-not-killed files move to what_conforms, which is the field that already means 'changed to match'.

B: the SCHEMA gains a third list (what_changes), if the two rulings turn out not to be an authoring slip but a shape the schema cannot express. Do not reach for B before checking A — a schema change to explain one mistake is the expensive answer.

C: neither, and the rulings are confirmed as-is with the what_dies list understood as advisory. REJECTED IN ADVANCE and recorded so nobody re-derives it: ruling.py's tooth is not advisory, and a green packet whose instructions must be silently ignored is worse than a red one.
occurrences.gate_owed: The deeper finding, filed as an edge rather than fixed: NOTHING CHECKS A what_dies LIST AT INTAKE. `cairn ruling open` accepts any path string. A grep for importers of each dying file, run at intake and refusing a packet that sentences a file the corpus still imports, is the physics this trouble is the prose version of (Law 4). It is the same shape as the /sorted door refusing a drifted workflow string: one fix at the door costs one fix; the same error found at execution costs whatever the execution broke.

cleared_by.what_changed: RESOLUTION PATH A, taken. Both packets that carried the kill list are RETIRED, superseded by 2026-08-05-the-file-path-is-the-link-corrected, which Akien confirmed 2026-08-06 and whose what_dies is EMPTY. The re-read the trouble named as the first act was done: not one of his four verbatim lines names a file to remove. Path B (a third schema list) was NOT needed — the root cause was not an inexpressible shape, it was that what_conforms measured from the packet own INTAKE, so a ruling filed before its work landed had no green field but what_dies. Fixed at the door the same day: as_of names the commit ruled against, git renders the bytes, the door fingerprints THAT (cairn 9c93d91). The gate_owed — an importer scan refusing a packet that sentences a file the corpus still imports — is NOT built and does not clear with this; it stands as a filed edge on cairn/machines/ruling, which ruling 2026-08-01-edges-become-open-questions makes the open-question lane.
